identityAndEncryption.ingressKey: provider + environment + exact account/workspace + exact shop incarnation + provider event/message identity
identityAndEncryption.effectKey: effect type + exact shop incarnation + canonical command/result identity + provider account/capability
payloadBinding: canonical record and expected version when applicable
identityAndEncryption.rule: sensitive raw provider payloads and requests are encrypted; logs and diagnostics contain bounded redacted metadata only

sequence: authenticate provider or sidecar request and validate exact account, installation and shop authority
write the event to a sidecar durable spool before broadcast when the sidecar owns the provider socket
submit to authenticated app ingress with stable ingress key and encrypted raw evidence
commit new or duplicate database result before acknowledgement
commit Conversation, Message, audit, DomainEvent and automation-trigger intent atomically as applicable
publish websocket/UI change only from the database-committed result
retain quarantine, dead-letter, replay and reconciliation history
inbound.acknowledgement: the app acknowledges only after database commit; sidecar removal from spool occurs only after that acknowledgement
inbound.ordering: provider ordering is recorded but never trusted as the sole deduplication or checkpoint authority

outbound.attempts: every worker claim and provider call creates or updates immutable attempt history correlated to one effect key
outbound.preEffectRecovery: lease expiry before provider_call_started is safe to retry
outbound.postEffectRecovery: lease expiry after provider_call_started requires provider idempotency or receipt lookup; otherwise outcome becomes ambiguous
outbound.receipt: provider IDs, response hashes, timestamps and bounded normalized facts are durable before success is exposed
outbound.operator: ambiguous retry requires explicit duplicate-risk ceremony; reconciliation decisions are immutable and audited

automation.identity: stable trigger event identity + automation definition version
automation.stepPolicy: steps execute in declared order with explicit stop, continue or compensate policy
automation.truth: aggregate status is derived from persisted step states and can never report success after a failed required step
automation.effects: provider actions create shared durable effects and persist step-to-effect correlation
automation.recovery: leases, retries, dead letter, replay and operator decisions survive restart
automation.catalog: only validated trigger/action schemas with a committed producer and complete configuration may be activated

proposalBinding: affected record identities and expected versions
actor, member, device, session, installation and shop
proposal digest, issue time and expiry
ai.approval: one-time approval references the exact proposal digest and cannot authorize regenerated arguments
ai.execution: revalidate current authority and versions, claim approval once, execute canonical command, and persist result
ai.failure: tampered, expired, revoked, stale or already-used proposals fail closed

workerOwnership.policy: only the exact active native runtime drains its shop database
workerOwnership.switch: native shop switch quiesces workers, stops new claims and safely resolves or expires existing leases before runtime replacement
workerOwnership.inactiveShops: queued work remains durable and visibly pending; no hidden cross-shop worker or mutable global database selection is allowed

certification.authority: server-side capability certification and kill-switch state gates provider execution
certification.scope: provider + environment + account class + capability + API/contract version + evidence date
certification.rule: adapter presence, mocks or UI metadata never authorize production effects
certification.dhd: disabled in production until current live endpoint and behavior certification exists

experienceAndEvidence.diagnostics: redacted stable IDs, state transitions, attempts, error classes and receipt presence; no secrets or prohibited plaintext
experienceAndEvidence.retention: raw encrypted evidence and operational history use explicit bounded retention and preserve audit/reconciliation requirements

AR/FR/EN, RTL, accessibility and constrained-network states
